title: PowerPARK: Conceptualization of a standardized in-person and digital training program for people with Parkinson‘s disease and their relatives
summary:
Parkinson's disease is the second most common neurodegenerative disorder after Alzheimer's disease. It is characterized by both motor and non-motor symptoms.

For chronic conditions that require complex treatment and a high degree of self-responsibility—besides Parkinson's disease, such as diabetes, or multiple sclerosis—a well-structured and targeted training program is crucial. It helps patients and their relatives to manage the disease independently. Such training programs are an effective complement to medical treatment. In Germany, there is currently no such training program available for people with Parkinson's disease and their relatives.
To develop practical concepts, it is important to involve the perspectives of those affected and other stakeholders.

This project builds on this need. As part of this study, a modularly structured training program with both analog and digital components will be developed based on previous work and with the involvement of those affected and other stakeholders. In addition, the necessary infrastructural framework conditions will be established comprehensively. To this end, the perspectives of relevant groups (people with Parkinson's disease, relatives, caregivers, prospective trainers within the training program, and stakeholders within the healthcare system as study participants) will be collected through focus group discussions and document analyses and integrated into the further development of the training program. Furthermore, three co-creation workshops will be conducted to design the infrastructural framework conditions.

interventions.name:
One-time collection in separate focus group discussions with people with Parkinson's disease (n=8), relatives (n=8), caregivers (n=8), prospective trainers (n=8), and stakeholders (n=8).
For a one-time document analysis and three subsequent co-creation workshops, at least two participants per group

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Study Participants: People with Parkinson's disease (PwPD), relatives, caregivers, prospective trainers, cooperating stakeholders

PwPD: Diagnosis of Parkinson's disease (syn.: idiopathic Parkinson's syndrome, Morbus Parkinson); Ability to actively participate in a focus group discussion (FGD) with other patients for a maximum of 120 minutes (operationalized through self-assessment); German as a native language or very good German skills; Unrestricted or sufficiently corrected visual and auditory abilities; >18 years

Relatives: Interested persons with at least one relative with Parkinson's disease; Good or sufficiently corrected visual and auditory abilities; German as a native language or very good German skills; >18 years

Caregivers: Interested persons who are active in the health or social services (e.g., neurologists, nursing professionals, therapists) and are involved in the care of PwPD; Good or sufficiently corrected visual and auditory abilities; German as a native language or very good German skills; >18 years

Prospective Trainers: Interested persons who have professional or experience-based expertise with Parkinson's disease (e.g., organized self-help, caregivers); Good or sufficiently corrected visual and auditory abilities; German as a native language or very good German skills; >18 years

Cooperating Stakeholders: Interested persons who are active in the care or health services (e.g., health insurance companies, nursing support points, specialized clinics); Good or sufficiently corrected visual and auditory abilities; German as a native language or very good German skills; >18 years
Exclusion criteria:
Study Participants: People with Parkinson's disease (PwPD), relatives, caregivers, prospective trainers, cooperating stakeholders

PwPD: Dementia symptoms (investigated through the presence of a diagnosis)
Impairments of visual, auditory, and speech abilities that are not sufficiently corrected; Insufficient German language skills; <18 years

Relatives: Dementia symptoms (investigated through the presence of a diagnosis); Impairments of visual, auditory, and speech abilities that are not sufficiently corrected; Insufficient German language skills; <18 years

Caregivers: Impairments of visual, auditory, and speech abilities that are not sufficiently corrected; Insufficient German language skills; <18 years

Prospective Trainers: Impairments of visual, auditory, and speech abilities that are not sufficiently corrected; Insufficient German language skills; <18 years

Cooperating Stakeholders: Impairments of visual, auditory, and speech abilities that are not sufficiently corrected; Insufficient German language skills; <18 years
